clue.text: Tense quarrel after leader's demoted

indicators.note: in a down clue, demoting a letter means it drops lower down the column, two places here

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel
the leader is the first letter of the quarrel word, which is lifted out and put back lower

explanation.surface: An edgy row breaks out just after the boss has been pushed down the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of the quarrel word slides from the top down to third place.
explanation.definitionFit: The past is a grammatical tense, alongside present and future.

clue.text: Item passed down on radio broadcast tower

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the other
broadcast tells us to hear the word, so it is replaced by its sound-alike

parts.note: radio is the air, as in 'on air'
to loom is to tower over

explanation.surface: Something handed down the generations was announced on a radio programme from a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: An heirloom is a valued possession handed from one generation of a family to the next.

clue.text: Mum is coming over fast

indicators.note: coming over in a down clue suggests turning the word upside down

parts.note: taken as written
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: Mother is on her way over quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum looks like mother, but here it means keeping quiet, as in 'mum's the word'.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep mum is to stay quiet, so mum means saying nothing.

clue.text: Swift beasts fixed look over hawk coming north

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: a gaze is a long steady look

indicators.note: going north in a down clue means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: to hawk goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: A watcher fixes their stare on a hawk flying north, on the lookout for fast animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Hawk looks like the bird in this birdwatching picture, but it is the verb to peddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazelles are slender, fast-running antelopes of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Scrapped opening of obituary that's nasty in newspaper

indicators.note: these letters go inside the newspaper

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
ugh is the exclamation for something nasty

explanation.surface: An unpleasant start to an obituary in the paper was dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrapped looks like discarded, but it is the past of scrap, to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap is to brawl, so scrapped means had a fight.

clue.text: Light vehicle in America stopped deer, so Spooner says

indicators.note: Dr Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first sounds of the two words change places

parts.note: in American slang to can something is to stop it, as in 'can it'; said aloud, canned is a single syllable
a hart is a male red deer

explanation.surface: In the United States a small vehicle was halted by a deer on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of 'canned hart' gives 'hand cart'.
explanation.definitionFit: A handcart is a small cart pushed or pulled by hand, a lightweight conveyance.

clue.text: Crazy amount this account might show — unfathomable

indicators.note: crazy suggests something disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild sum appears on this bank statement, beyond anyone's understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of AMOUNT out of UNFATHOMABLE to leave FHABLE, then rearrange them. 'This ... might show' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: 'On my account' and 'on my behalf' both mean for my sake or in my interest, so the nouns are interchangeable.

clue.text: Simple home requires fences

indicators.note: the words enclose the answer, as a fence encloses a field

parts.note: the answer sits across the end of home and the start of requires

explanation.surface: A plain house needs fencing round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means nothing more than, as in 'a mere child', so it matches simple in the sense of only.

clue.text: Sheep gathering around after a drink

indicators.note: the sheep piece follows the A

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: gathering means holding the other letters within it

parts.note: the merino is a breed of sheep prized for its wool
CA is circa, Latin for around

explanation.surface: Sheep cluster round after someone has had a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An americano is a coffee drink made by diluting espresso with hot water.

clue.text: TV presenter Richard having no tips for singer

indicators.note: the tips are the end letters, which are dropped

parts.note: Richard Madeley is a British daytime television presenter

explanation.surface: A television host called Richard, minus his tips, becomes a singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is a multi-award-winning English pop vocalist.

clue.text: Nit perhaps beset by wound in Roman province's running event

indicators.note: the built piece goes inside the province

parts.note: Thrace was a province of the Roman Empire in the Balkans

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by the next word

parts.note: wound here is the past of wind, as of reeling in a line
a nit is the egg of a louse, so an example of an egg

explanation.surface: A louse egg wound up in a Roman province during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Wound rhymes with sound, not with spooned: it is the past tense of wind, here reeled.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-legged race is a sports-day contest where partners run with two legs tied together.

clue.text: King aboard vessel with aluminium exterior

definitions.note: a noun here; the answer is mostly an adjective, though it can also mean a facade

indicators.note: the letter is on board, inside the vessel word

parts.note: a font is a vessel for baptismal water

explanation.surface: A king on a ship clad in aluminium.
explanation.walkthrough: Vessel suggests a ship, which King and aboard support; it is the church basin.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontal is the facade of a building, so its outside face.

clue.text: Conducive to thrill abandoning stream for river

parts.note: for can mean in favour of or helping towards

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving the next word out

parts.note: taken as written, before the stream is removed
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: For a thrill, someone leaves a little stream for a big river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forth is a Scottish river flowing into the Firth of Forth at Edinburgh.

clue.text: Upset tons with rebuke

indicators.note: joins the two pieces in order

parts.note: to give someone an earful is to scold them

explanation.surface: Plenty of telling-off left someone distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tearful is crying or close to tears, as an upset person is.

clue.text: Gave wrong information holding note that's wrinkled

indicators.note: the first word holds the note within it

parts.note: to lie is to give false information

explanation.surface: A liar kept hold of a crumpled note.
explanation.definitionFit: A lined face is creased with age, the same as a wrinkled one.

clue.text: Title to divine German tale?

definitions.meaning: reads like a name for a god, but means a name that must be guessed
the Grimm brothers' folk tale in which the queen must guess the imp's name

explanation.walkthrough: In the Grimms' story the queen must divine the little man's name, which is also the title of the tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The imp's name is both the riddle the heroine must solve and the title of the Grimms' fairy story.

clue.text: One despatched from base, girl on a railway

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms
a miss is a young woman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl sent from headquarters is travelling on a train line.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is a messenger or agent sent on a mission.

clue.text: Sides of invention fold up

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its outer letters

parts.note: taken as written; only its first and last letters are kept
a crease is a fold line

explanation.surface: The edges of a gadget fold upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Up looks like part of the phrase 'fold up', but it stands alone as the verb to raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To up prices is to raise them, so up as a verb means to make bigger.

clue.text: Big profits from book about misfortune

indicators.note: about means wrapped round the next piece

parts.note: Kings is a book of the Old Testament
ill as a noun is harm or bad luck

explanation.surface: Huge gains come from a book concerning bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a killing is to make a large financial gain.

clue.text: Be seen leaving Aberdeenshire rum that's plundered

indicators.note: rum in its British sense of odd or peculiar signals that the remaining letters are rearranged
be seen leaving says the letters of these words are taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: Someone is spotted leaving a Scottish county with stolen rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the stolen drink; it means odd. Aberdeenshire is a Scottish county; removing B, E, S, E, E, N leaves ARDEHIR to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Harried in its older sense means raided and laid waste, the same as plundered.

clue.text: Type of film from Hammer, say, set in space

indicators.note: the rapper is placed inside the space word

parts.note: room means space, as in 'room to move'
MC Hammer is a rapper, an example of an MC

explanation.surface: A kind of movie from the Hammer horror studio, set in outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: Hammer suggests the British horror studio Hammer Films; it is the rapper MC Hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A romcom is a romantic comedy, a genre of cinema.

clue.text: Cut around East End

indicators.note: around means the word is turned the other way

parts.note: diced means cut into cubes

explanation.surface: A clipped instruction about London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: East End suggests the London district; End is the definition, as in settling a matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide a dispute is to settle it, bringing it to a conclusion.

clue.text: Players directed and made changes on board

parts.note: the cast are the actors in a production
led means guided or directed

explanation.surface: Actors were directed and altered the boards they performed on.
explanation.walkthrough: Board suggests the stage; it is the chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Castling is the chess move that shifts king and rook together in a single turn.

clue.text: Kept feeding pig, constant companion

indicators.note: feeding means going into the next word

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
had means kept or held

explanation.surface: A farmer kept feeding a pig that followed them everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A shadow is someone who follows another person everywhere, an inseparable follower.

clue.text: Politicians in private, most cautious banning outsiders

parts.note: at home, as in 'is she in?'
secret means private or hidden

indicators.note: the outside letters are removed

parts.note: wariest means most cautious

explanation.surface: Politicians meeting privately, at their most guarded, keep outsiders away.
explanation.walkthrough: In looks like a link to 'in private'; it gives the first piece on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Home Secretaries are UK government ministers in charge of the Home Office.

clue.text: Legwear selected, but no top

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, here removed

parts.note: chose means selected

explanation.surface: Stockings were chosen, but no top to go with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose is a collective word for stockings and tights.

clue.text: Elite soldiers, hard band

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service, the British army's special forces regiment

explanation.surface: Crack troops form a tough group.
explanation.walkthrough: Band looks like a group of soldiers; it is a strip of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a long strip of fabric worn round the waist or over a shoulder.

clue.text: First of Camorra dons turned clean

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the word is clothed by the next

parts.note: milk that has turned has gone sour

indicators.note: the first of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the Camorra is the Neapolitan mafia; only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: The head of the Camorra mafia's bosses went bad and cleaned up.
explanation.walkthrough: Dons look like Mafia bosses; it is the verb to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour is to clean by hard scrubbing.

clue.text: Moves from position and avoids being pierced by missile oddly overlooked

indicators.note: the other letters go through the middle of the word

parts.note: dodges means avoids

indicators.note: the odd letters are skipped, keeping the even ones

parts.note: taken as written; only its even letters survive

explanation.surface: Someone shifts position and dodges being struck by a missile that missed.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge is to knock or force something out of its place.
